pos.personaBrief: Scheiberlspiel, short flat combinations and the Calciomercato 'possesso palla' claim show a possession side that wanted the ball and controlled play.

pro.personaBrief: Hogan helped Meisl drop aerial passing for groundwork, and Austria played flat short passes (Austria-Forum, Wikipedia), so patient build-up over direct play.

est.personaBrief: Close one-two combinations and a withdrawn Sindelar point to relational play, though the 2-3-5 with natural wingers (1931 line-up) is a fairly set shape.

lar.personaBrief: The 1931 line-up had two natural wingers (Zischek, Vogl) but the style centred on short combinations through Sindelar, Schall and Gschweidl in the middle.

blo.personaBrief: No verified evidence; from general knowledge, 1930s Austria was an attacking, ball-playing side with no pressing culture or deep block, and it wanted to play its game.

mar.personaBrief: No verified evidence on Austria's own marking; from general knowledge, the era's defending leaned individual, with only the opponent's man-marking of Sindelar (Monti 1934) documented.

pla.personaBrief: 'Spüts euer Spüü' and the Danubian waltz against Pozzo's man-marking show a team playing its own way whatever the opponent.

res.personaBrief: Danubian football was admired as a style and Meisl told the team to play its game even when 0-2 down at Stamford Bridge, so spectacle over result.

sis.personaBrief: The Wunderteam was built around the brain and freedom of Sindelar, 'no brawn but any amount of brain', and Meisl yielded to the press to field him, so talent decides.

jog.personaBrief: Sindelar the Paper Man and the attacking centre-half Smistik show a preference for technique and intelligence over strength; Meisl is credited with Scheiberln over British kick and rush.

bas.personaBrief: In 1931 Meisl rebuilt the side with debutants and Vienna players, but a national team has no academy and the title-winning core was seasoned; mixed, leaning experience.

lid.personaBrief: Meisl was a raging authority figure who dropped Sindelar in 1929 for answering back, yet yielded to journalists' pressure in 1931; boss over harmony.
